headline: H.Res. 590 was a 2019 House resolution that would have formally disapproved of the Speaker starting an impeachment inquiry without a full House vote; it did not pass.
what_it_does: The resolution would have stated the House's disapproval of the Speaker's decision to open an impeachment inquiry into President Trump without a debate or vote by the full House on an impeachment inquiry resolution. It was a question of privileges, a procedural tool that lets any member bring a matter affecting House rights to the floor. Because it was tabled, it would have expressed the House's position but would not have changed any law or government program.
